name: llmtrim
hint: compresses whole requests via a local HTTPS interceptor; installs a local CA, sets HTTPS_PROXY in shell profiles and runs a login daemon
trims: Whole request payloads: conversation history, tool schemas and tool outputs, plus a terse-output instruction. A local HTTPS interceptor compresses every request before it leaves the machine.
helps: Long sessions with large histories and many tools, on any agent that honours HTTPS_PROXY. Its own A/B benchmark reports large cuts with quality checks; it is self-run, so measure your own bill.
caveats: System-level: a private CA in ~/.llmtrim, HTTPS_PROXY and CA variables in your shell profile (HKCU on Windows), a login daemon, and Claude Code hooks/subagents it adds itself. All LLM traffic is decrypted locally. Not supported: Copilot (certificate pinning), Cursor Agent, Kiro. Single maintainer.

commands.desc: Check the install end to end; --fix applies repairs
Launch one agent (claude, codex, …) through the interceptor
Start or stop the background interceptor
Stop running the interceptor at login
Where the local CA certificate is and how to trust it
Update to the latest release and refresh integrations
Undo everything setup did (--purge also drops the savings ledger)
